prompt: A Cook–Levin encoding keeps every pairwise “not both symbols” clause but omits the “at least one symbol” clause for a cell. What invalid setting is now allowed?

options.text: Two symbols in that cell simultaneously
options.explanation: The retained pairwise clauses still forbid that.

options.text: A symbol from outside the machine alphabet
options.explanation: There are no variables for symbols outside the fixed alphabet in this construction.

options.text: No symbol in the cell at all
options.explanation: Setting all its symbol variables false satisfies every pairwise not-both clause.
Omitting a clause does not change the machine’s fixed alphabet.

workedExample: The remaining pairwise clauses say that no two symbols can both be selected. They do not require any symbol at all. Setting every cell-symbol variable false satisfies them, leaving a cell with no symbol. The missing at-least-one clause is needed to describe an actual configuration.
